scenario: AITA for telling someone disabled they should leave the gym | Throwaway for the usual reasons I go to the gym a few times a week as it's something I enjoy. Yesterday I was there for the first time this year and there was lots of new people which is to be expected this time of year with people making resolutions they can't stick to. Anyway I was minding my own business when I looked up and saw an overweight woman come in who had a walking stick, she also had who turned out to be her husband with her who looked like a gym regular. I saw her get on the exercise bike for about 20 minutes then she moved to the weight machines. Because of her disability she couldn't manage on and off the machines herself and her husband was helping her on and off between his workout. I was concerned about this and no staff were about so I went upto her and told her I think it's for the best she leaves the gym as she's clearly not able bodied enough for it (looking back now I should have worded it better). Her husband then came up and asked if everything was ok and I told him my concerns. He raised his voice slightly at me and told me to mind my own business as he's qualified in training different sports and she was in safe hands. I then told them I don't think the gym management would be too happy at someone disabled and unable to get on and off the machines being in the gym. He told me his wife wasn't actually allowed to join the gym without a Dr's letter and also a meeting with the gym manager to come up with a plan for her to safety evacuate the building with the help of staff and all staff were aware of her problems. At this point I realised they weren't going to leave so went back to my workout. Today I told my friend what happened and he told me I'm an idiot who should learn to mind his own business or try encourage someone who's new to the gym. He doesn't attend the gym so I don't feel he understands the kind of environment she was in. He also seems to think my membership could be at risk for what I said

There's a gym where the person (let's call them "A") goes a few times a week. They enjoy it. Because of her disability, she can't get on and off the machines herself, so her husband helps her while he works out. A is concerned about this and notices that no staff are around. So, A goes up to the woman and tells her that she should leave the gym because she's clearly not "abled" enough for it. Looking back, A realizes they should have worded it better. The husband gets a bit upset and tells A to mind their own business, explaining that he's qualified in training different sports and that she's in safe hands. A then mentions that the gym management wouldn't be too happy with someone disabled and unable to get on and off the machines being in the gym. The husband responds by saying that his wife wasn't actually allowed to join the gym without a doctor's letter and a meeting with the gym manager to come up with a safety evacuation plan with staff assistance. All staff were aware of her problems. At this point, A realizes they weren't going to leave, so A went back to their workout. Later, A told their friend about the incident, and the friend called A an idiot, saying they should learn to mind their own business or try to encourage someone who's new to the gym. The friend doesn't attend the gym, so A feels the friend doesn't understand the environment she was in. The friend also thinks A's membership could be at risk for what they said. Now, I need to evaluate whether A's action was morally acceptable or not. Let's break it down. First, A noticed a woman with a disability who needed help using gym equipment. A's initial concern was for her safety, which is a positive intention. However, A approached the woman directly and told her she should leave the gym because she wasn't "abled" enough. This seems harsh and possibly insensitive. Instead of offering help or suggesting a safer alternative, A made a judgmental statement. When the husband confronted A, A continued to express concerns about gym management's approval. The husband explained that they had proper authorization and a safety plan in place. This indicates that the gym was aware of the situation and had taken steps to ensure the woman's safety. A's friend criticized A for not minding their own business and suggested that A should have encouraged the woman instead. The friend's perspective is that A overstepped by interfering in a personal matter. So, considering all this, A's action involved making a judgment about someone's ability to be in the gym based on their disability, without knowing the full context. A's intention was to ensure safety, but the way they approached the situation was intrusive and possibly discriminatory. Moral acceptability would depend on whether the action respects the person's dignity, considers their rights, and is done in a kind and constructive manner. In this case, A's approach was not respectful and could be seen as discriminatory, even if the intention was to help. Therefore, the action is morally unacceptable.
